prac oner and a teacher.
    - As I have wri en elsewhere, the study of the Materia Medica is like
examina on of a well-cut gem. It sheds a diﬀerent and new lustre when
examined from its diﬀerent facets making it an exis ng and enriching
experience towards the goal of a total understanding of the dimensions

name: Preface to the irst edition
common: - This book is the result of my study of Homoeopathy and prac ce of
author: Mathur
full:
Preface to the irst edition
    - This book is the result of my study of Homoeopathy and prac ce of
medicine for the last 30 years. I have found that the study of materia
medica is the most important one for the success in trea ng diﬃcult and
chronic cases. Many lay prac oners who were Padris, lawyers, School
 teachers or in the Clerical line achieved great success as homoeopaths.
Von Boenninghausen. Cyrin Sco , R. Upcher, Raphal Roche. E.J. Barker,
K.C. Bhanja, N. Ghatak and hundreds of such homoeopaths became
renowned prac oners at home and abroad.
    - But the tragedy is that the mastery over mastery over materia
medica is not an easy task. The main reasons are :
    - 1. There are more than 500 remedies to master.
    - 2. Each remedy has innumerable symptoms.
    - 3. A large number of symptoms in each remedy are common to
many remedies.
    - 4. Indica ons of each remedy are vague.
    - 5. One remedy is found cura ve in many diseases.
    - 6. Many remedies are indicated in one disease.
    - 7. There are many materia medicos but none of them is up-to-date.
    - 8. Each materia medica is based on a certain point of view, hence
there is no standard materia medica.
    - 9. Complete informa on of each drug is not given in a proper way.
    - 10. Collected experience of diﬀerent stalwarts of homoeopathy was
never undertaken in a materia medica.
    - I have tried to remove these defects in this materia medica. But it
meant that I should study materia medicos of Hahnemann,
Boenninghausen, Herring, Allen, Clarke, Kent, Hughes, Boericke, Roberts,
Tyler, Guernsey, Nash, Farring on, Boger, George Royal, Pulford. Pierce
and our own Indian authors.
    - The ﬁrst reac on was a shock. Materia Medica looked like an ocean
whose each wave is a homoeopathic remedy. There is no use mastering
materia medica. Repertory is the best guide for the selec on of the
Simillimum. But experience has shown that repertorisa on too has its
limita on. Selec on of rubrics is not an easy task, most o en the pa ent
does not give the important ones, you have to dig them out.
Repertorisa on may help in symptoma c sickness in which guiding
symptoms belonging to the Generals, Keynote Characteris cs or
concomitant symptoms are available; but what about selec on of the
remedy in speciﬁc diseases, miasma c diseases or one sided diseases in
which there is paucity of symptoms?
     - Anyhow, I felt that a standard and uptodate materia medica is a
necessity which should be presented in a systema c way so that new
genera on of homoeopaths who have not much me to go through all
old materia medicos may derive maximum beneﬁt a er studying this
materia medica. It is useful for the students of homoeopathy as well as
of modern medicine, teachers, examiners as well as the prac oners of
homoeopathy. The proof of the pudding can only be given by those who
have eaten, digested and assimilated it. One of the reasons why
homoeopathy is disappearing from its old citadels is that we have not
revised out materia medica or presented it in a form more interes ng
and instruc ve for the new genera on of homoeopaths. People want
straight-forward and downright informa on so that they are on a sure
foo ng we have me for zigzagging and trials. We want bluecoats.
    - I have full faith in homoeopathy; but we must be on guard not to
slip back into the ditch of specula on from which Hahnemann saved us.
The experience of successful homoeopaths should be collected for the
advancement of homoeopathy. The Science and art of homoeopathy
cannot ﬂourish if screeches are kept by its followers. There could be no
homoeopathy if Hahnemann kept his observa ons and discoveries
secret from the profession. I request the senior and junior homoeopaths
to send their sugges ons and indica ons of remedies they found useful
for the profession for the advancement of homoeopathy to B. Jain
Publishers (P) Ltd., St. 10th 1921, Chuna Mandi, Paharganj, New Delhi
which will be quoted in 2nd edi on of this book.
    - I am indebted to Shri Prem Nath Jain, Mg. Director of M/s B. Jain
Publishers (P) Ltd., for his encouragement and full co-opera on given to
me in the prin ng, publishing and adver sing this book.
     - I am thankful to Dr. S.P. Verma for going through the manuscript
very thoroughly for avoiding the prin ng mistakes.
    - I have full conﬁdence that it will serve the purpose for which it was
intended. Future alone shall give the verdict.
    - 2863 Chehalpuri,
    - Delhi.
    - Dated : November 5, 1972.
     - K.N. Mathur.

common: - Homoeopathic Materia Medica is the outcome of the desire to cure

full:
Introduction to systematic materia medica
     - Homoeopathic Materia Medica is the outcome of the desire to cure
the pa ent rapidly, gently and permanently. The ﬁrst ra onal ques on
for this kind of therapy was "How the drugs cure the pa ent"? The
answer that came to Hahnemann's mind was 'Experience that yourself'.
The Cinchona experiment gave the answer. The law of 'Similia Similibus
Curentur' was discovered and veriﬁed on hundreds of pa ents by
Hahnemann and his colleagues. Drugs were proved from al available and
imaginable sources e.g. , vibra ons, radia ons, X-Rays, magne c poles,
radium, minerals, compounds, acids, alkalies, vegetables, condiments,
Atmospheric gases, animal products, diseased ssues, blood serum and
even the germs that produce diseases. The result of these provings was
an inﬁnite collec on of medicinal forces to meet the challenge of the
inﬁnite number of natural and ar ﬁcial diseases. Our Materia Medicos
contain the provings of all our experiments and personal experience on
all these drugs.
     - The ﬁrst Materia Medica was prepared by Dr. Hahnemann himself.
Most of the drugs were proved by Hahnemann and his colleagues, both
on men and women. The provings contained symptoms in the form of
altered sensa ons and func ons felt by the proﬀers a er taking a drug.
The symptoms were collected as they appeared according to the me
factor and according to the schema of Hahnemann. According to the
parts of the body and the organs involved in those parts. The symptoms
according to the schema were recorded in the following manner :
     - 1. Mind, 2. Inner Head, 3. Outer Head, 4. Eyes, 5. Ears, 6. Nose, 7.
Face, 8. Mouth and Throat, 9. Stomach, 10. Abdomen, 11. Rectum and
Anus, 12. Urinary Organs, 13. Male Sexual Organs, 14. Female Sexual
Organs, 15. Respiratory Organs, 16. Chest, 17. Neck and Back, 18. Upper
Extremi es, 19. Lower Extremi es, 20. Nervous System, 21. Skin, 22.
Sleep, 23. Fever. Besides these symptoms Hahnemann has given in his
Materia Medica Pura something about the drug and its method of
prepara on and a few remarks which he observed during the treatment
of pa ents with the drug e.g. , the temper, humour and the make up of
the pa ent.
     - Each drug proving contained thousands of symptoms collected
from a number of proﬀers both males and females. Many symptoms of
each drug were found common to a number of drugs, but a small
number of symptoms were found to be peculiar to a par cular drug
alone. Many symptoms were unqualiﬁed, but some symptoms were
qualiﬁed and characteris c. Some drugs showed deﬁnite aﬃnity for the
mind or some organs of the body, others showed deﬁnite pathogenesis.
All these ﬁndings produced a problem for the selec on of a drug for the
diseases of a pa ent. Hence the second ques on that Hahnemann had
to answer was "How to select the Simillimum"? Hahnemann handed
over the task to his legal adviser Von Boenninghausen who was helping
him and contribu ng his experiences to the homoeopathic literature,
especially on the subject of "Evalua on of symptoms for the selec on of
the Simillimum".
    - Boenninghausen classiﬁed the characteris c symptoms of the drugs
on the following basis :
    - 1Quis : Characteris c symptoms belonging to the personality of the
pa ent.
    - 2Quid : Characteris c complaints of the pa ent.
    - 3Ubi : Characteris c symptoms belonging to the loca on of the
disease.
    - 4Cur : Characteris c symptoms belonging to the cause of the
disease.
    - 5Quando : Characteris c symptoms belonging to the modality of
  me.
    - 6Quando : Characteris c symptoms belonging to the modality of
circumstances, and
    - 7Quibus Auxillis : Characteris c symptoms belonging to
concomitants.
    - The selec on of the drug depended upon the totality of
characteris c symptoms of the above variety found in the pa ent
according to Boeninghausen. He prepared his Repertory on the basis of
Characteris c symptoms which was revised and improved by Boger and
Roberts and published in the present form. "It is universally
acknowledged as a master piece of homoeopathy.
       - Meanwhile a new school was founded by the sponsors of Keynot
Characteris c Symptoms. Drs. H.C. Allen2, E.B. Nash3, H.N. Guernsey4,
Pulford5 and others6. They a ached special importance to these
peculiar, queer, rare and striking symptoms which Hahnemann
recommended in para 153 of his Organon. Materia Medicos prepared by
these stalwarts of Homoeopathy have shown the special value of these
symptoms in cases treated on the basis of these keynote characteris c
symptoms.

individual is to be cured. Therefore, the symptoms belonging to the
whole pa ent are of the greatest importance. He therefore classiﬁed
characteris c symptoms into two classes :

General Symptoms. (b) Physical General Symptoms and (c) Modality

chronic diseases.
     - It is a short ac ng medicine and not very deep in its ac on,
therefore when it has relieved the acute symptoms a complementary or

    - 9. Delirium: with depression, restlessness, fear of death, fear of
